text: The Patriots are preparing for a bruising Week 2 matchup against Pittsburgh's vaunted defense with both encouraging news and fresh injury concerns on the roster front. Running back TreVeyon Henderson declared himself "ready to go" after sitting out the season opener with an ankle injury, and he'll be joined by wide receiver Efton Chism III making their debuts against the Steelers, though the team took an early hit when starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off with an ankle injury late in the first quarter on Sunday. The organization also marked a bittersweet moment as legendary cornerback Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro, signed a one-day contract to retire as a member of the Patriots. All eyes will be on second-year quarterback Drake Maye as he faces the challenge of balancing the patience and aggression that New England's offense demands against a Steelers team that's rolling, making Sunday's home opener at Gillette Stadium a crucial early-season test.
